chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn al-Rabi', from Ali ibn Khattab, from the muezzin of the Red Mosque, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is there in the Book of Allah a similitude for the Qaim (peace be upon him)? He said: Yes, the verse of the owner of the donkey; Allah made him die for a hundred years, then raised him up.

key_terms.اللْقَائِم: The Rising One, referring to the Twelfth Imam
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْحِمَارِ: The Owner of the Donkey, a title for the figure in Surah Al-Baqarah

ai.seo_question: What Quranic verse serves as a precedent for the Imam of the Age's long lifespan?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to establish a direct Quranic typology for the Qaim's occultation, linking the miraculous preservation of the man in Surah Al-Baqarah to the Imam's hidden longevity. This connection underscores the theological validity of the Ghaybah by grounding it in a well-known scriptural precedent of death and resurrection after a century. The reference serves to reassure the Shia community that the Imam's prolonged absence is a divinely ordained state of preservation rather than a loss.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 405 - It is narrated by Himyari from his father from Ja’far bin Muhammad Kufi from Ishaq bin Muhammad from Qasim bin Rabi from Ali bin Khattab on the authority of the Muezzin of the red mosque:

I asked Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s), “Is there in the Book of Allah a similitude for the Qaim?” He said: “Yes, the verse of the owner of the donkey, Allah made him die for a hundred years and then raised him up again.”
